title: Collection and Staining Analysis of Vaginal Smears
author: Roberta Marongiu

steps.title: Prepare and label slides
steps.instruction: Pre‑label each glass slide with study number, animal number, date and time of collection using a permanent marker; arrange the slides on a suitable tray, grouping slides by collection date (one set of slides for all females each day).

steps.title: Collect vaginal sample
steps.instruction: Hold the mouse by the base of the tail and lift its back slightly; moisten a cotton‑wool tip of a sterile swab by dipping it into a jar of saline or distilled water and sharply flick off any surplus; insert the swab at an angle of about 45° to the animal’s body and rotate the swab in a single direction to collect cells; keep the swab almost horizontal and gently roll the tip onto the pre‑labelled slide below the relevant animal number, avoiding excessive pressure that would leave too much fluid or urine on the slide; discard the used swab and use a fresh swab for each animal; let the slide dry completely on a horizontal surface for 5–10 minutes before staining.

substeps.instruction: Hold mouse by tail base and lift back slightly
Moisten swab tip in saline or distilled water, flick off excess
Rotate swab at ~45° angle to collect cells
Roll swab tip horizontally onto labelled slide, avoiding excess fluid and urine
Discard swab; use a new swab for each animal

steps.title: Set up staining solutions
steps.instruction: Transfer each Hema‑3 solution (Fixative, Solution I, Solution II) into separate Coplin jars; keep the Fixative jar covered when not in use to prevent methanol evaporation.

steps.title: Stain slides with Hema‑3
steps.instruction: Dip each dry slide 5–10 times for approximately one second per dip in Hema‑3 Fixative Solution; immediately dip the slide 5–10 times for one second each in Hema‑3 Solution I; then dip 5–10 times for one second each in Hema‑3 Solution II; rinse the slide briefly with de‑ionized (DI) water; staining intensity can be altered by changing the number of dips in Solution I (eosinophilic) or Solution II (basophilic).

steps.title: Analyze vaginal cytology
steps.instruction: Examine the stained slide under a microscope to assess the presence and proportion of the two types of epithelial cells, cornified (keratinized) cells, and leukocytes; classify the estrous stage as a single stage (E, M, D, or P) if within normal appearance, or as a transitional stage (e.g., MD or DP) if features of two stages are present; remember the normal 4–5‑day cycle follows the sequence M → D → P → E repeatedly; note occasional mucus in acyclic females.
